claim.why_it_matters: The ISO title-page banner lost the words "INTERNATIONAL" and "ISO/IEC", so the transcription's title page reads "STANDARD 1989" instead of naming the document as International Standard ISO/IEC 1989. Front matter only; no normative content is affected.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 3 prints a two-column title banner: 'INTERNATIONAL / STANDARD' on the left and 'ISO/IEC / 1989' on the right. The page-3 markdown's first content line is just 'STANDARD 1989'. Neither 'INTERNATIONAL' nor 'ISO/IEC' appears anywhere else in the banner text. 'ISO/IEC 1989:2002(E)' does appear lower down, but only in the reference-number line. The OCR dropped the top line of each column. Both sources are quoted accurately. The words are genuinely missing; this is not a case of reflow or hyphenation. The banner is title-page content, not running header or footer furniture. The cosmetic severity is right: the page is front matter with no normative effect, and the reference number still identifies the document.
